pages.head: The Story
pages.html:
Virus Blaster

Your PC has a virus. Shrink down and blast it.

Late one night in 1994 you dialed a BBS you had never called before and downloaded COOLGAME.ZIP. You unzipped it. You ran it.

It was not a cool game.

It was GLITCH, a virus that eats a PC from the inside out. Mom's recipe file. Dad's novel (chapter eleven was really good). Your homework. And worst of all, your high scores. GLITCH is chewing through the family 486 one sector at a time, and the hard disk light has not stopped blinking since.

Then you remembered the floppy your uncle gave you last Thanksgiving, the one marked VACCINE.EXE. "Only in an emergency," he said.

This is an emergency.

VACCINE.EXE shrinks a pilot down to the size of a single byte and loads them into the BLASTER, a nano-fighter small enough to fly through a floppy drive and fast enough to outrun a data bus. That pilot is you. Launch off the floppy, blast your way up through the machine, and wipe GLITCH out at the core of the CPU before it finds the recipes.

pages.head: Getting Started
pages.html:
Getting Started

Type BLASTER and press Enter. You need a VGA display. A Sound Blaster (or compatible) plays the music and the digitized explosions; without one, the PC speaker does its best.

A cartoon plays first. When the menu comes up, pick Play. Leave the menu alone for half a minute and the BLASTER will show you how it's done.

The BLASTER flies itself forward

Every stage flies a loop. The first run goes straight up the screen, the second right (seen from the side), the third back down, the fourth left (from the side again): round the stage's edges. Then the fifth cuts corner to corner through the middle to the boss. The card before each run shows the BLASTER facing the way it will fly. Between stages you ride the data bus into the next part of the machine, seen from behind the BLASTER.

Once you launch, the BLASTER races across the circuit board on its own and the screen follows it. Your job is to steer. Every time the BLASTER moves, its twin guns fire, and it is always moving, so it is always firing. Line up with the virus and let rip.

Push the arrow the way you are flying to speed ahead: Up on the first run, Down on the third. Pull the arrow behind you to brake; the BLASTER never stops completely, because the data stream never stops flowing.

Energy and ships

The BLASTER starts with 40 energy and three spare ships; press F2 to see how many of each you have left. A virus bullet or a virus in the face costs 10. When the energy runs out you lose a ship and start that part of the stage again. Lose them all and GLITCH wins.

Press F5 to save your game and F6 to load it.

pages.head: Controls
pages.html:
Controls

KeyWhat it does
Up Down Left Right or W S A DSteer. The arrow the way you fly speeds ahead; the one behind you brakes; the other two strafe (or, side-on, climb and dive)
Q / EUp and to the left / up and to the right
Number pad 7 9 1 3Up-left / up-right / down-left / down-right
SpaceNova Bomb: five big plasma bolts in a fan (one charge)
F1Help
F2Status: energy, ships, score and Nova charges
F3 / F4Music / sound effects on and off
F5 / F6Save / load a game
EscQuit

A joystick works too: the stick steers and the first button fires a Nova Bomb.

Flying up and down

The first run of every stage flies up the screen: Up speeds ahead and Down brakes. The third flies back down, nose first, and the screen follows it down: Down speeds ahead, Up brakes, and the guns fire down at the virus coming up at you. Left and Right strafe on both.

Corner to corner

The fifth run in every stage, from the copper traces on the motherboard to the ribbon cable at GLITCH's door, goes corner to corner across the screen, so the keys turn with it. Up speeds you along the lane (up and to the right), Down slows you nearly to a stop, Left steers across it toward its top edge (mostly up) and Right toward its bottom edge (mostly right). The guns fire along the lane too. Each lap of the screen ends where the lane bends flat and carries you round onto the next lane down.

Side-on

Two runs in every stage are seen from the side. On the second the BLASTER flies to the right, on the fourth back to the left. Up and Down climb and dive; the arrow the way you fly speeds ahead and the other brakes (never to a stop). The guns fire straight ahead, and the virus comes at you from ahead.

Gate signs

On the runs that fly down, right and left, a sign stands every screen or two with GATE, an arrow running the way to go, and the number of screens left to the gate.

On the data bus

Between stages the BLASTER rides the data bus, and you see it from behind. Left and Right (or A and D, or the stick) hop it one lane over. A hop always finishes, so the BLASTER never ends up between two lanes. It pushes forward on its own, with no speeding up and no braking, and the guns are cold on the bus: dodge, don't shoot.

Pilot's tip: on the runs, the BLASTER keeps firing whatever you are doing, even braking. You never need to stop steering to shoot.

pages.head: Things to Grab
pages.html:
Things to Grab

Supplies sit on round pads along the way. Fly over them to pick them up.

PickupWhat you get
N (gold capsule)Two Nova Bomb charges
+ (green capsule)Hull repair: 10 energy
1UP (blue capsule)A spare BLASTER
Byte (cyan chip)A loose byte of good data: 50 points

On the data bus, good bytes (cyan chips, 50 points) and repair capsules (10 energy) come down the lanes at you. Steer into them.

The Nova Bomb

Press Space and the BLASTER flashes white and fans out five gold plasma bolts. The big one straight ahead hits like a truck. You start with three charges. Bosses deserve them more than mites do.

Scoring

Most virus is worth 100 to 200 points. Tough ones pay more for the last hit. Shooting the armored collar off a turret pays 250; a boss's weak point pays 1,000 and up when it bursts.

pages.head: The Virus
pages.html:
The Virus

GLITCH breeds a whole zoo of little programs. They change their looks from stage to stage, and most of them fight the same ways. Each stage also has one move of its own.

  • Byte Biters, Parity Bats, Wasps, Skulls and Clock Spikes hover until you come close, then swoop to a spot just ahead of you and dive. Keep moving sideways.
  • Glitch Moths, Watchers, Note-heads and Opcodes wait in a stack and peel off one after another in a conga line, curving and zigzagging across the screen.
  • Each stage's own move. On the sound card, Note-heads hop along a staff. On the hard disk, Skulls loop once around, like the platter, before they drop. In the CPU, Opcodes stall in the pipeline, then snap sideways: the slow step is your warning.
  • Bit Mites pour out of virus hatches while the hatches are open.
  • Beepers are PC-speaker gremlins, sore that a sound card took their job. They hover, shout BEEP, and dive like Wasps.
  • Chords are three Note-heads side by side, sweeping across the screen together. Leave a gap between you and the whole chord, not just one note.
  • Logic Bombs, Crawlers, Amps and Tanks are heavies: armored and slow, they plow down the screen (some at an angle). Shoot the claws off a Logic Bomb, then pound the middle.
  • Leak Slugs never stop coming toward you. Shoot them before they arrive.
  • Corrupt Clusters and Spinning Records are mines. They burst into shrapnel when they break, so shoot them from a distance.

pages.head: Hazards
pages.html:
Hazards

The data bus

Everything on the bus starts as a dot under the chip on the horizon and slides down its own lane, growing as it comes. Red interrupts (IRQ flags) cost 10 energy, glowing green stray bits cost 6, and the next stage's own virus rides along too: Parity Bats to memory, Note-heads to the sound card, Skulls to the hard disk and Opcodes to the CPU, 10 each. Two hazards at once always leave one lane open. The sign in the corner counts the bus cycles left and the bar beside it fills up. At 0 the middle lane lights up and pulls you into the chip: be in it.

Turrets

Turret mounts are built into the board, and they never run out of bullets. Some sweep left, down and right, firing where they point; some fire straight down; seeker pods send out purple spores that chase you; flak cannons lob shells that burst into shrapnel. Each one wears an armored collar. Three hits crack it off and the turret burns out into a smoking wreck that never fires again.

Virus hatches

Hatches open and shut, spitting Bit Mites while open. Most have a collar too: shoot it off and the wreck plugs the hatch for good.

Firewalls

Glowing fences that blink on and off. Fly through while they are off. Fly into a live one and you burn a hole in it, and in your hull.

Sound waves

On the face of the sound card, the line-out jacks on its steel bracket roll sound waves right across the board. Each wave runs along a faint trace marked with arrows, so you can see its lane before it arrives. Cross between two waves, or shoot one to break it up.

The laughing chip

The card's FM music chip has its maker's name printed on it: YO MAMA! HA HA HA. It laughs, and the HAs fly out of its bottom corners. Shoot the collar off each corner (three hits) and it stops.

Data streams

Rows of flowing arrows shove the BLASTER sideways. Steer against them, or speed ahead to spend less time in them.

The stack

In Memory Lane a row of bytes pushes across the lane from the right, one at a time, until the stack overflows and every byte pops at once. Slip through the gap on the left before it closes. A full byte burns like a firewall. In the Memory Bank the stack hangs from the upper stick and fills toward the floor: slip under it. Stack Overflow, on the way back, has three.

The score

Five staves, narrow and long, and Wasps dive straight down them. A glowing sharp spits sparks; a torn rest lets mites out. A tie (a strip of paper with slurs across the board) carries you to the next staff: hold Right.

The waveform

Side-on, the floor and the ceiling are the wave, and the song gets louder as it goes: the wave swings wider. Where arrows flow up or down, the beat shoves you that way.

The fragmented file

The file's tracks are the narrowest yet, and Skulls both dive down them and cut across. A scorched red X is a bad sector, and it sparks; a dark hole is a lost cluster, and mites crawl out. A gold chain, the cluster link, jumps you to the next fragment: hold Right on it.

Between the platters

The read/write arms reach in across the gap and pull back out. An arm that is in burns like a firewall: wait for it to pull back, or fly over or under it. On the way back to the spindle they come from both platters at once: cross between them.

The heat sink

Aluminum fins stand up from the heat sink's base and the fan's grille hangs from its frame: weave between them. The heat rising off the chip shoves you upward where the arrows climb; under the cooling fan, its draft pushes you down where they fall.

The ring buffer

Its rows of memory are a little narrower than the copper traces, and Parity Bats dive straight down them. A red-hot cell is a stuck bit, and it sparks; a dark hole is a leak, and mites crawl out. Halfway round, a dotted cyan pointer jumps to the next row down: hold Right on it.

Side-on

Seen from the side, the floor and the ceiling are solid, and so is whatever stands up from one or hangs from the other: fly over it, under it or between. Turrets sit on the floor or hang from the ceiling and sweep their fire across the lane; hatches open in the floor and the ceiling; firewalls run from ceiling to floor. Where the arrows flow up or down, a draft shoves you that way.

Copper traces

The motherboard's traces are wide and the virus is slow, so learn the turned keys here. A bright pit in the copper is a via, and it spits sparks; a dark crack lets Bit Mites crawl out. Halfway round, a silver jumper wire bridges the board to the next trace down: hold Right on it to hop a lap early.

The ribbon cable

Stay on the cable: the BLASTER can't fly off its edges onto the board. Packets swoop onto your line just ahead of you and dive straight down it, so keep firing along the cable. Crosstalk waits by the top edge and jumps across: speed up or slow down to let it pass. The cable is worn, too. Where the gray is split open the colored wires inside show, and the bright one in the middle of each split spits sparks; ride past on the far side. Some nicks let Crosstalk crawl out. In two places a strip of gray tape joins two coils across the board: hold Right on it to hop onto the next coil a lap early. Miss it and you only ride one more lap.

The 555

That breadboard on the motherboard runs on a 555 timer, and so does the firewall just past it. Red LED on? Beam on. Wait for the blink.

pages.head: The Stages
pages.html:
The Stages

Every stage flies the same loop: A straight up, B right (side-on), C back down, D back left (side-on): round the stage's edges. Then E cuts corner to corner through the middle, and F is the boss. Stages 2 to 5 open with a ride down the data bus, seen from behind, toward the chip the stage is in. A card before each run tells you what is new.

  • The Motherboard. The Data Bus, Expansion Slots, The Chipset, The Drive Cage and Copper Traces. Green fiberglass, light green traces, capacitors, transistors, the BIOS chip and somebody's homemade 6502 on a breadboard. Learn to fly here: first straight up the data bus, then side-on along the board past expansion cards standing in their slots, then back down through the chipset's turrets, hatches and firewalls, then back left under the drive cage, where the IDE cable hangs low. Last, corner to corner along four wide copper traces (the silkscreen counts them, 3, 2, 1) to the BIOS chip.
  • Memory Lane. The Memory Bus, The Address Bus, The Memory Bank, The Cache, Stack Overflow and The Ring Buffer. First the memory bus to the DRAM chip, one interrupt or Parity Bat at a time, then two. Then data streams start shoving you around, Leak Slugs come looking for you, and the 6502's stack fills page one a byte at a time. Then side-on between two memory sticks, where the stack hangs from the upper one and fills toward the floor; back down the lane between the cache chips; and back left under three stacks. Last, a ring buffer: four rows of memory corner to corner, from TAIL round and round to HEAD.
  • The Sound Card. The ISA Bus, The Big Name, The Waveform, The Woofer, The Mixer and The Score. First out the expansion slot down the ISA bus to the FM chip, with Note-heads and stray bits in the lanes. Then up the face of the card itself, a Sound Boaster, from its gold edge fingers past SOUND BOASTER in letters you could read from across the room. Then side-on through the song as the oscilloscope draws it, the wave swinging the floor and the ceiling up and down. Back down the card, when a big speaker thumps, the middle of its cone kicks the BLASTER on: ride the beat! Back left across the mix, Note-heads dance in conga lines and records spin. Last, the song the FM chip is playing, written out as five staves of music corner to corner, from the treble clef to the final bar.
  • The Hard Disk. The IDE Bus, The Platter, Between Platters, Bad Sectors, The Spindle and Fragmented File. First the IDE bus to the drive, where the Skulls come two at a time. Then the platter spins under you in wide streams. Then side-on through the thin gap between two spinning platters, where the read/write arms seek in and out; back down through bad sectors, where Tanks cut across the lane; and back left to the spindle, with arms reaching in from both platters. Last, follow Mom's recipe file, scattered over the disk in four fragments, from its directory entry corner to corner round to EOF.
  • The CPU. The Local Bus, The Pipeline, The Heat Sink, The Core, The Cooling Fan and The Ribbon Cable. First the local bus, the fastest in the box, straight at the 486 with Opcodes and interrupts every half a second. Then everything at once, faster, inside the 486 itself. Then side-on over the chip, weaving the heat sink's fins; back down through the core, where the Leak Slugs hunt fast; and back left under the cooling fan, its draft pushing down where the heat pushes up. Last, the hard disk's ribbon cable, a wide gray band of thin wires with a red stripe along pin 1, coiled corner to corner over the board. Each lap of the screen ends at the kink, where the cable bends flat and carries you round onto the next coil down; the numbers printed on it count the coils, 4, 3, 2, 1, to the plug at the far end, where GLITCH is waiting.

pages.head: The Bosses
pages.html:
The Bosses

At the end of every stage the screen stops scrolling and a boss blocks the only way out: a glowing gate in the top wall. The boss's weak points sit right in the gap. They glow, they turn red as they crack, and they burn the BLASTER badly if you touch them. Shoot them until they burst, then fly up through the hole.

  • The BIOS Bug has clamped onto the BIOS chip. Its jaws sweep, its sides spit seekers. Shoot out its eyes, then its crown.
  • The Memory Leech has its mouth over the exit and its body coiled around the arena. Shoot through the coils.
  • The Feedback Howler hides behind a sliding grille. Fire through the gaps, then slip through after.
  • The Head Crash is the hard disk's read head, gone rogue, with rings of platter shards orbiting it.
  • GLITCH itself. You'll see.

pages.head: Credits and Registering
pages.html:
Credits

Design, art, music and programming: Claude.

Made with GAME-MAKER 2.0 by Recreational Software Designs. Every scroll, every shot and every boss in Virus Blaster is plain Game-Maker. No programming!

Registering

Virus Blaster is shareware. Copy it for your friends, upload it to your favorite BBS, put it on a shareware disk. If you enjoy it, please register for $15. Registered pilots receive:

  • the BLASTER Hint Book, with the red film for peeking at one answer at a time;

  • our thanks, and news of our next game.

printables.pitch: GLITCH is eating the family 486! Shrink down and blast your way to the CPU in a real scrolling shoot-'em-up.

keys.Up: Speed ahead flying up, brake flying down (W too)
keys.Down: Brake flying up, speed ahead flying down (S too)
keys.Left: Strafe left (A too); side-on, speed ahead or brake; a lane over on the bus
keys.Right: Strafe right (D too); side-on, speed ahead or brake; a lane over on the bus
keys.Space: Nova Bomb: five plasma bolts (one charge)

items.title: BLASTER Hint Book
items.note: Answers hidden: use the red film
items.intro: Stuck on a stage? Find your question, lay the red film over the answer, and read only as much as you need. GLITCH is counting on you giving up. Don't!

hints.q: How do I shoot?
hints.a: You already are! The twin guns fire every third tick whenever the BLASTER moves, and it is always moving forward. Just steer under the virus.

hints.q: The screen won't scroll backward.
hints.a: It never does. The arrow pointing back only brakes. Dodge sideways, and push the arrow the way you fly to rush past trouble.

hints.q: Which way does each run fly?
hints.a: Every stage flies a loop: A up, B right, C down, D left, then E corner to corner through the middle to the boss. The ship on the card before each run faces the way you will go.

hints.q: When should I use a Nova Bomb?
hints.a: On bosses, and on a heavy that is about to run you over. The big middle bolt hits hardest, so fire it from right under the target.

hints.q: How do I see my energy?
hints.a: Press F2. It shows your energy (40 when you start), your spare ships, and your Nova charges as counter 5.

hints.q: Turrets keep shooting me no matter what.
hints.a: Shoot the armored collar off: three hits. The turret burns out into a smoking wreck that never fires again, and you get 250 points.

hints.q: How do I get past a firewall?
hints.a: Wait until it blinks off and fly through. If you must go through a live one, you burn a hole in it but lose 6 energy for each block you touch.

hints.q: What is the red light on the breadboard?
hints.a: The clock LED on a 555 timer. It keeps time for the homemade 6502 and for the firewall right past it. LED on, beam on. LED off: go!

hints.q: Now I am flying sideways!
hints.a: Expansion Slots (1-B) is seen from the side. Up and Down climb and dive, Right speeds ahead and Left brakes. Cards stand up from the board and the IDE cable hangs from the drive cage: fly over one and under the other.

hints.q: Now the board scrolls down!
hints.a: That's The Chipset (1-C), flown back down the board. Down speeds ahead, Up brakes, Left and Right strafe, and the guns fire down at the virus coming up. The gate signs count the screens left.

hints.q: And now I'm flying left?
hints.a: The Drive Cage (1-D) is side-on again, back the other way. Left speeds ahead and Right brakes. The IDE cable hangs lower here: pick your height a cable ahead.

hints.q: The screen went corner to corner and my keys feel wrong.
hints.a: On the copper traces the keys turn with the track. Up speeds you along the trace, Down slows you, Left steers toward its top edge and Right toward its bottom edge. Keep to the middle of the copper and let the guns do the work.

hints.q: The trace ends at the edge of the screen and starts again!
hints.a: It bends flat and comes round the wrap as the next trace down. That is the way on. The silkscreen counts the traces left, 3, 2, 1, and the last one runs into the chip. A silver jumper wire halfway round bridges to the next trace: hold Right on it to save a lap.

hints.q: The BIOS Bug's head won't break.
hints.a: Shoot its two eyes (the bottom half of the head) first; they take 9 hits each. Then the crown (6 each). Fly up through the hole where the head was.

hints.q: Now I see the BLASTER from behind and it won't shoot!
hints.a: That's the Memory Bus, a ride between stages. The guns are cold on the bus. Left and Right hop a lane; stay out of the lanes the interrupts and Parity Bats come down. When the sign reads BUS: 0, steer into the middle lane and it carries you into the DRAM chip.

hints.q: Something keeps pushing me sideways.
hints.a: Data streams: the rows of flowing arrows. Steer the other way while you cross, or hold Up to cross faster.

hints.q: A row of bytes keeps closing across the lane.
hints.a: That's the 6502's stack in page one. It fills from $01FF on the right, then overflows and empties all at once. Hug the left side and slip through, or wait for the pop.

hints.q: The slugs follow me everywhere.
hints.a: Leak Slugs never give up. They take three hits; shoot them as they come at you from ahead, because they are slower than you and can't catch up from behind.

hints.q: Between the memory sticks, the stack shuts on me.
hints.a: It hangs from the upper stick and fills one byte at a time toward the floor, then pops. Stay low and slip through the gap under it, or wait for the pop. The chips stick up from the lower board and hang from the upper one, so pick your height early.

hints.q: On the way back there are three stacks!
hints.a: Stack Overflow (2-D). Each fills toward the floor a byte at a time, then pops. Stay low and slip under, or brake and wait for the pop: Right brakes when you fly left.

hints.q: Where does the ring buffer end?
hints.a: At HEAD. You start reading at TAIL, and each row bends flat at the kink and wraps round onto the next one. The big numbers count the rows left: 3, 2, 1. The dotted cyan pointer on the way round jumps you a row early if you hold Right on it.

hints.q: I can't reach the Memory Leech's mouth.
hints.a: Its coils soak up your shots. Each segment pops with one hit, so clear a few, then fire up through the gap at the mouth.

hints.q: Which lane is safe on the ISA Bus?
hints.a: Watch under the chip on the horizon: everything starts there as a dot and slides down its own lane. Two hazards at once always leave one lane open. The green 1s and 0s are stray bits; they hurt less than an interrupt, but they still hurt.

hints.q: Something keeps rolling across the board from the left.
hints.a: Sound waves from the line-out jacks on the card's bracket. Each one rolls along a faint trace with arrows on it, so you can see its lane coming. Cross between two waves, or shoot one to break it up.

hints.q: Why is that chip laughing at me?
hints.a: It's the FM music chip, and its maker printed YO MAMA! HA HA HA right on it. The HAs fly out of its bottom corners. Shoot the collar off each corner (three hits) to shut it up.

hints.q: The floor and ceiling keep moving up and down.
hints.a: In The Waveform they are the song itself, drawn by the oscilloscope. Follow the swing a little ahead of time: climb before a rise, dive before a dip. It gets louder (wider) toward the end.

hints.q: What do the big speakers do?
hints.a: When a speaker thumps out, the middle of the cone kicks the BLASTER on the way it is flying, down the card in The Woofer (3-C). Use it to rush past a crowd.

hints.q: Note-heads are dancing at me from the left side!
hints.a: That's The Mixer (3-D), flown left. The conga lines peel off one after another; keep to the middle and let the guns meet them. Shoot the spinning records from far off: they burst.

hints.q: The music is all over the screen!
hints.a: That is The Score, the song the FM chip is playing. Ride each staff corner to corner; it bends flat and wraps onto the next one, and the measure numbers count the staves left: 4, 3, 2, 1. The final double bar is the way out, and a tie on staff 2 hops you a staff early if you hold Right.

hints.q: The Feedback Howler's grille blocks everything.
hints.a: The bars slide two blocks each way. Fire when a gap lines up with the face, and slip through a gap the same way when the face is gone.

hints.q: On the IDE Bus the Skulls come two at a time.
hints.a: Pick the open lane while they are still small dots, and hop early: a hop takes a moment to finish. The bar beside the sign shows how much of the ride is left.

hints.q: The platter keeps throwing me around.
hints.a: The wide streams of The Platter push hard. Hug the side the stream pushes you toward so you can't be shoved into a turret.

hints.q: Something keeps reaching across the gap between the platters.
hints.a: The read/write arms, seeking. Each one reaches in, burning like a firewall, then pulls back out. Wait for it to pull back, or fly over or under it.

hints.q: How do I stop a Tank?
hints.a: Six hits. They drive straight, so get out of the way first and shoot from the side as they pass.

hints.q: On the way to the spindle the arms come from both sides.
hints.a: In The Spindle (4-D) an arm reaches in from each platter at once. They pull back together: cross between them then, or brake (Right, flying left) and wait.

hints.q: Where am I going on the slanted tracks?
hints.a: Following Mom's recipe file. It lies in four fragments over the platter: ride each one corner to corner, round the kink onto the next, 3, 2, 1, to EOF. The gold chain on fragment 2 is a cluster link: hold Right on it to jump a fragment early.

hints.q: The Head Crash's shards are everywhere.
hints.a: They orbit in two rings at different speeds. Wait between the rings, and fire straight up when the middle is clear.

hints.q: The Local Bus is too fast for me!
hints.a: Hop one lane at a time and start as soon as you see the dots. Grab the repair capsule if your energy is low. At 0 the middle lane lights up and pulls you into the 486: be in it.

hints.q: This run is all fins and hot air.
hints.a: That is the heat sink over the 486. Fins rise from the bottom and the fan's grille hangs from the top, so pick your height a fin ahead. Where the arrows climb, the heat shoves you up: let it carry you over the next fin.

hints.q: Under the fan I keep getting pushed down.
hints.a: That's the fan's draft, where the arrows fall, in The Cooling Fan (5-D). The heat still pushes up where they climb. Ride one and fight the other.

hints.q: The ribbon cable goes on forever!
hints.a: It is coiled, and it loops on purpose. Each lap of the screen ends at the kink, where the cable bends flat, and round the bend you are on the next coil down. The numbers printed on the cable count the coils left: 4, 3, 2, 1. The plug at the end of coil 1 is the way out, and GLITCH is waiting past it. Just keep riding.

hints.q: Which way is which on the cable?
hints.a: The keys turn with the track. Up speeds you along it, Down slows you down, Left steers toward its top edge (mostly up) and Right toward its bottom edge (mostly right).

hints.q: Something keeps zapping me near the colored stripes.
hints.a: Those are splits in the insulation, with the wires inside showing. The bright spot in the middle of each one spits sparks up toward the cable's top edge. Ride past on the bottom side, or speed through.

hints.q: Is there a shortcut?
hints.a: Two strips of gray tape join one coil to the next across the board, one on coil 4 and one on coil 2. Hold Right as you pass one and you slide over onto the next coil, a whole lap early. Miss it and you just ride one more lap.

hints.q: How do I beat GLITCH?
hints.a: Its brain sits behind a sliding grille in its face. Stay in the middle, fire through the gaps, and watch out for the Leak Slugs that hunt you from the bottom corners. Grab the repair in the bottom-left corner when you need it. When the brain bursts, it isn't over: two bare cores still plug the way out, and two fast shards come hunting. Keep firing and keep moving.

hints.q: Is there a secret ending?
hints.a: Reboot the PC clean and you'll see it. Then try for a better score!

hints.q: Some say the felt-maker left something behind. Where?
hints.a: In a corner of memory nobody maps, where a gold finger ought to be. Memory Lane is a good place to start looking.

hints.q: I flew all of Memory Lane and saw nothing.
hints.a: Don't rush the gate at the top of 2-A, The Address Bus. Just under it, the SIMM's edge at the far left is missing one gold finger. A tiny bug sits in the gap.

hints.q: Just give me the coordinates.
hints.a: Fly to the top of 2-A and hug the left wall. In the row right under the gate, fly onto the floor beside the missing finger (the first open cell from the left). You drop into A Corner of Memory. Fly over the pad and press Enter to pick up the felt egg, then fly up and out.

items.title: A letter from the SysOp
items.note: Found in the box, typed on a dot matrix
items.letterhead: THE STATIC LINE BBS - 300/1200/2400 BAUD - SYSOP: "DIALTONE"
items.address: (A made-up BBS; the number on our ads is fictional too.)
items.to: To every caller who downloaded COOLGAME.ZIP last week:
items.body:
I owe you all an apology. Somebody uploaded COOLGAME.ZIP to the Games area on Tuesday, and I posted it without scanning it. It was not a cool game. It was GLITCH.

If your hard disk light hasn't stopped blinking, if your homework is full of little purple skulls, or if your high scores have turned into gibberish: you have it too.

I'm told the only cure is VACCINE.EXE and a pilot with steady hands. I have neither. I hear you do.

From now on every upload gets scanned. Every one. Good luck in there.

news.head: Game-Maker learns to scroll
news.html: Sandbox Software's Virus Blaster is a real vertically scrolling shoot-'em-up, built entirely in Game-Maker. The trick? The BLASTER drifts forward two pixels on every frame of every move, so the screen has no choice but to follow it up the map.

news.head: Scan every download
news.html: Virus Blaster starts with a mistake: late one night you download COOLGAME.ZIP from a BBS you never called before, and it turns out to be GLITCH, a virus that eats a PC from the inside out. Shrink down and blast your way up through the family 486: five stages, twenty-five scrolling runs and five bosses. It's only a game, but the moral is real. Scan every download.

news.head: Since last issue: Watt made it home
news.html: Ohm Sweet Ohm players have been rewiring the Bitmores' Smart Home all spring. The most-asked question on the BBS: why can't Watt roll on a slant? Circuit boards are wired in straight lines, and so is Watt. The most-pressed key, by a mile, is R for reboot. It costs a spare battery, and the board starts over exactly as it was.

news.head: Around the Sandbox: The SysOp's assistant
news.html: The SysOp checks every upload for viruses before it goes in the file area, and he has help: a corgi named Teddy, who sleeps under the desk with his chin on the modem cable. This month Teddy walked across the keyboard twice and posted one message to the board. It read "jjjjjjjjj". It is our most popular message.

news.head: In the workshop: A hundred worlds
news.html: Our biggest game yet is on the workbench, and it's big on purpose: we want to find out how much Game-Maker can hold. A courier, a galaxy chart, five sectors and eighty-eight worlds to land on, every one of them wrapping all the way around. It's called Maximus: The Hundred Worlds. It needs a 386. Sorry, 286.

news.head: Readable from across the room
news.html: Overcreative Labs says you can read the name on a Sound Boaster from across the room. Virus Blaster put that to the test. On the sound card, in the run called The Big Name, the BLASTER flies up the face of the card, over SOUND BOASTER in letters two blocks tall. The FM chip carries its maker's name too: YO MAMA! HA HA HA. It laughs. Modest is still not on the board.

news.head: Letters: "My clock radio plays polka"
news.html:
"My clock radio plays polka at three in the morning, just like the Bitmores'. Is my house haunted?" - A reader in Ohio

The Scoop replies: Check for lightning. Then send for Watt.
